notes.meaning: The writer cries out to God from deep waters, a picture of crushing sorrow and distress over his sin. He realizes he cannot rescue himself from this pit, so he directs his voice straight to the Lord. Honest prayer often starts in the darkest places of life.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Known by its opening Latin words as the De Profundis, this psalm is one of the seven traditional penitential psalms and is regularly prayed for the dead in funeral liturgies and evening prayers.

notes.meaning: The psalmist begs the Lord to listen attentively to his cry for mercy. By calling God his Master and Ruler, he acknowledges that God has full authority over every problem he faces. He does not claim to deserve help, but humbly asks for God's unearned favor.

If God kept a strict record of every wrong thought and action, no human being could survive His judgment. To stand refers to a courtroom setting where someone is declared innocent and acquitted. Since every person has broken God's law, no one could stand innocent on their own.

God offers real pardon, and that mercy leads people to revere and honor Him instead of running away in terror. The fear of God here is not slavish dread, but a loving and childlike awe that hates to offend such a good Father. Knowing that God forgives inspires genuine worship and holiness rather than careless sin.

The psalmist waits with his whole heart for the Lord to bring relief and assure him of pardon. He anchors his hope entirely in God's written word, trusting promises that cannot fail. This kind of waiting is not lazy sitting around, but an active, confident trust in God's timing.

The writer longs for the Lord more eagerly than night watchmen long for the break of day. A watchman on duty never doubts that morning will arrive; he only waits through the dark hours until the dawn appears. In the same way, the believer waits through dark times with total certainty that God's light and comfort will come.

Having found peace himself, the psalmist calls on the whole nation to put their trust in the Lord. God's loyal love is boundless, and His ability to redeem, or buy back His people from slavery to sin, has no limit. Believers are pointed to look directly to the Lord Himself rather than just the blessings He gives.

differ.view: God's redeeming mercy belongs especially to His chosen church, the elect, rather than to the whole world.
God's abundant redemption is sufficient and offered to all people who will turn to Him and accept it.

notes.meaning: The Lord Himself will set His people free from all their guilt and rebellion. This promised rescue covers not only the painful results of sin, but the grip and power of sin over the human heart. It points forward to the full spiritual salvation that God provides for all who trust Him.
